correctness.rationale: The positive real Jacobi matrix has simple spectrum and cyclic lossy endpoint, so the non-Hermitian generator is strictly stable and integrated survival solves an exact Lyapunov equation. Its energy-basis diagonal and off-diagonal identities force an exact alpha/gamma+beta*gamma law for real initial vector; reflection symmetry gives alpha=m. A fixed-m rank-one Schur complement reduces beta to an odd alternating chain. Its nonzero sine modes contribute 2(m-1)a^2/b^2 and zero mode contributes (b/a)^(2m-2), giving the stated beta including m=1. Independent actual Gramian checks for 24 parameter combinations m=1,2,3,4,5,7 had max relative deviation 1.7e-13; m=1 separately symbolic. Optimization follows by convexity in gamma.
residual_risks: Numerical checks finite; general conclusion relies on reviewed fixed-size Lyapunov and explicit singular-mode argument.

value.rationale: Single-endpoint loss and transport across finite SSH chains are natural physical observables. The exact all-m time and unique optimal loss give a substantive geometric zero-mode contribution and exponential-versus-linear optimized scaling; it is not a renaming of the uniform chain or another numerical spectral-gap plot.
residual_risks: Fixed a,b before m large; no disordered or many-body generalization.

final_claim: For 2m alternating SSH sites with hoppings a,b>0, one endpoint loss -i gamma at site 1 and initial opposite endpoint, T_m=m/gamma+gamma[(m-1)/b^2+b^(2m-2)/(2a^(2m))]; optimized lifetime scales exponentially when b>a and linearly otherwise.
limitations: Only fixed finite even chain and one imaginary endpoint loss, real hopping and pure one-particle evolution.
Conclusions are about integrated survival, not universal Liouvillian spectral gap.
